snapshot.summary:
- Purpose: E‑commerce demo/catalog page for browsing products, viewing product details, adding items to a shopping cart, and accessing account, help and API/testing resources.
- Main flows: navigate categories (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS and subcategories), open product detail (View Product), add items to cart (Add to cart → View Cart), signup/login and proceed to checkout; access Test Cases/API Testing/Video Tutorials/Contact Us pages.
- Other actions: filter by brand (brand names with product counts), view cart summary, navigate site header links.
- Key UI elements to test: header navigation links, category and brand filters, product cards, View Product modal/page, Add to cart button behavior, View Cart page, Signup/Login forms, Contact/Help pages, API list page.
- Edge case — cart behavior: adding same item multiple times, quantity updates, cart persistence across refresh or login/logout, removing items, empty cart handling.
- Edge case — data consistency: brand count vs actual items shown, price/total calculation, promotions or zero/negative quantities, out-of-stock or deleted products.
- Edge case — auth flows: guest checkout vs logged-in, session expiry during checkout, invalid/duplicate signup, forgotten-password flows.
- Edge case — resilience: slow/failing API responses, broken links/icons (e.g., special icon text " Products"), missing images, malformed product data.
- Edge case — UI/UX: responsiveness on mobile, truncated labels, pagination/large result handling, keyboard accessibility and ARIA/assistive tech support.

snapshot.summary:
- Purpose: product listing/catalog page to browse all products, filter by category/brand, view product details, and add items to the shopping cart.
- Primary flows: navigate site (Home, Products, Contact us, Test Cases, Video Tutorials, API Testing), filter by category (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS), filter by brand, click View Product for details, click Add to cart and View Cart, use Signup / Login for account-required actions, use #scrollUp to return to top.
- Key UI interactions: product tiles with Add to cart and View Product buttons, category/brand links with item counts, site-wide header navigation links.
- Important edge cases — functional: Add to cart when item has variants/quantity not selected, Add to cart from listing vs product page (consistency), attempting cart actions when not logged in, empty filter results, pagination/infinite-scroll load failures.
- Important edge cases — data/state: out-of-stock or inventory mismatch after adding, cart/session persistence across refresh/login/logout, duplicate rapid-clicks adding multiples, price/discount mismatch between listing and detail.
- Important edge cases — environmental/accessibility: JS disabled or slow network causing broken Add/View actions, broken links for header items, responsive layout hiding buttons on small screens, #scrollUp anchor behavior on long pages.

snapshot.summary:
- Main purpose: allow users to create accounts, sign in, and subscribe to newsletters; acts as the authentication entry point and gateway to shopping pages.
- Main user flows: Signup (create account), Login (authenticate), Newsletter subscribe, navigation to Home/Products/Cart/Test Cases/API Tutorials/Contact pages, and page scroll-up.
- Key interactive controls: Login and Signup buttons, subscribe button, multiple form inputs including #susbscribe_email.
- Input/validation flows to test: empty fields, invalid email formats, password length/complexity, leading/trailing whitespace, max-length and very-long inputs, duplicate-email signup.
- Authentication edge cases: incorrect credentials, case-sensitivity, account lockout/rate-limiting, password reset absent/visible, session persistence and logout behavior.
- Security and injection checks: SQL injection/XSS in form fields, CSRF on forms, behavior under rapid repeated requests.
- UI/UX and robustness: responsiveness across viewports, keyboard/tab order and focus, error message clarity, button disabled/enabled states, network error handling and form state after navigation.

snapshot.raw_html:

APIs List for practice

Below is the list of APIs for you to practice the API testing in Automation. Click on the scenario for detailed API:

API 1: Get All Products List

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/productsList
  • Request Method: GET
  • Response Code: 200
  • Response JSON: All products list

API 2: POST To All Products List

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/productsList
  • Request Method: POST
  • Response Code: 405
  • Response Message: This request method is not supported.

API 3: Get All Brands List

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/brandsList
  • Request Method: GET
  • Response Code: 200
  • Response JSON: All brands list

API 4: PUT To All Brands List

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/brandsList
  • Request Method: PUT
  • Response Code: 405
  • Response Message: This request method is not supported.

API 5: POST To Search Product

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/searchProduct
  • Request Method: POST
  • Request Parameter: search_product (For example: top, tshirt, jean)
  • Response Code: 200
  • Response JSON: Searched products list

API 6: POST To Search Product without search_product parameter

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/searchProduct
  • Request Method: POST
  • Response Code: 400
  • Response Message: Bad request, search_product parameter is missing in POST request.

API 7: POST To Verify Login with valid details

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/verifyLogin
  • Request Method: POST
  • Request Parameters: email, password
  • Response Code: 200
  • Response Message: User exists!

API 8: POST To Verify Login without email parameter

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/verifyLogin
  • Request Method: POST
  • Request Parameter: password
  • Response Code: 400
  • Response Message: Bad request, email or password parameter is missing in POST request.

API 9: DELETE To Verify Login

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/verifyLogin
  • Request Method: DELETE
  • Response Code: 405
  • Response Message: This request method is not supported.

API 10: POST To Verify Login with invalid details

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/verifyLogin
  • Request Method: POST
  • Request Parameters: email, password (invalid values)
  • Response Code: 404
  • Response Message: User not found!

API 11: POST To Create/Register User Account

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/createAccount
  • Request Method: POST
  • Request Parameters: name, email, password, title (for example: Mr, Mrs, Miss), birth_date, birth_month, birth_year, firstname, lastname, company, address1, address2, country, zipcode, state, city, mobile_number
  • Response Code: 201
  • Response Message: User created!

API 12: DELETE METHOD To Delete User Account

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/deleteAccount
  • Request Method: DELETE
  • Request Parameters: email, password
  • Response Code: 200
  • Response Message: Account deleted!

API 13: PUT METHOD To Update User Account

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/updateAccount
  • Request Method: PUT
  • Request Parameters: name, email, password, title (for example: Mr, Mrs, Miss), birth_date, birth_month, birth_year, firstname, lastname, company, address1, address2, country, zipcode, state, city, mobile_number
  • Response Code: 200
  • Response Message: User updated!

API 14: GET user account detail by email

  • API URL: https://automationexercise.com/api/getUserDetailByEmail
  • Request Method: GET
  • Request Parameters: email
  • Response Code: 200
  • Response JSON: User Detail

Feedback for Us

  • We have identified above scenarios and added in the list.
  • You can explore more test cases in the website and if you find new test scenario that is not covered in above list, do let us know. We will definitely add that in above list.
  • If you think, this website should cover up any particular feature, kindly share with us at feedback@automationexercise.com. We will work on that part. Your feedback matters a lot.

snapshot.summary:
- Main purpose: a catalog page listing available API endpoints for the Automation Exercise site so testers can discover and exercise endpoints (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) such as products, brands, search, login, register, and user account operations.
- Main user flows: navigate site menu (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Contact); select an API entry to view/use that endpoint; perform API actions (GET product list, POST search/login/register, PUT/DELETE for update/remove); sign up/login for endpoints that require authentication.
- Key endpoints to exercise explicitly: Get All Products, POST/PUT/DELETE on Brands, POST Search Product, POST Verify Login, POST Create/Register, DELETE/PUT user operations, GET user account details.
- Important edge cases — malformed/partial labels and truncated UI text (verify full names and links resolve correctly).
- Missing/duplicate URL labels (multiple items show the same base URL) — validate each endpoint target and parameterization is unique and correct.
- Authorization-required flows: test authenticated vs unauthenticated access, token expiry, invalid or missing credentials.
- Input validation: invalid JSON, missing required fields, excessive payload size, SQL/JS injection attempts, and boundary values for search/filter parameters.
- HTTP method edge cases: method not allowed responses when using wrong methods, unexpected status codes (500, 404), and inconsistent response schemas.
- Network/CORS and rate limiting: simulate slow/failed connections, CORS restrictions, and rate-limit behavior.

snapshot.summary:
Purpose: a catalogue page that lists and links to the site’s predefined functional test cases (Test Case 1–20) for QA/reference.

Main user flows: navigate via top menu (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases), open individual test-case details, follow external/internal links (e.g., site root), and use flows referenced by test cases (register/login, search, add to cart, place order, contact form).

Concrete actions to validate: clicking each test-case opens the correct details; top-nav highlights/redirects work; truncated titles either expand or show full text/tooltip; links open in same or new tab as expected.

State-dependent flows to test: test-cases that require authentication (register/login, place order) should handle authenticated vs unauthenticated users and redirect or prompt appropriately.

Form-related flows: Contact Us, subscription, search and login forms need validation for valid/invalid/empty inputs, special characters, and large payloads.

Cart/order flows: adding/removing items, quantity updates, empty-cart behavior, checkout for registered vs guest users, concurrency (duplicate submissions).

Edge/negative cases: broken or 404 links, slow network/timeouts, session expiration, permission errors, duplicate submissions, DB/state cleanup between tests.

Accessibility/responsiveness: menu collapse/hamburger behavior on small screens, keyboard navigation, tooltip/aria for truncated titles, and cross-browser rendering.
